operations.name: Debug Profile
operations.description: Read the persistent native or .NET debug/run profile. runtime selects automatic/native/dotnet; dotnet selects an installed host or automatic discovery. Adapter/process access is required because the profile can contain environment variables.

cwd.description: Workspace document reference; not a temporary input artifact.

operations.name: Debug Configure
operations.description: Update and atomically save supported debug profile fields in .cycode/launch.json. Arguments are argv elements, not a shell command. Does not compile or start a program.

cwd.description: Workspace document reference; not a temporary input artifact.

operations.name: Debug Status
operations.description: Read actual DAP state, verified breakpoints, threads, stack, scopes, variables, watches and bounded adapter output. Source lines/columns are one-based. Runtime identifiers expire on resume/relaunch.

operations.name: Debug Breakpoints
operations.description: Replace source breakpoints for one workspace file and persist them. Supports enabled flags, conditions, hit counts and logpoints according to adapter capabilities. expectedBreakpoints rejects concurrent changes.

path.description: Workspace document reference; not a temporary input artifact.

operations.name: Debug Launch
operations.description: Launch a trusted native executable or runnable .NET assembly through DAP. Automatic runtime detection uses PE/CLI metadata and apphost companions; .NET uses NetCoreDbg and a compatible installed dotnet host. Defaults to the saved profile; supplied fields override this launch. The GUI separately provides build-before-debug. Requires matching debug symbols. Managed output uses the debug console; use debug_run for interactive stdin.

cwd.description: Workspace document reference; not a temporary input artifact.

operations.name: Debug Attach
operations.description: Attach to the explicitly supplied process ID through DAP. Stop/disconnect detaches attached processes instead of terminating them. OS permissions and adapter support still apply.

cwd.description: Workspace document reference; not a temporary input artifact.

operations.name: Debug Run
operations.description: Run a trusted native executable or runnable .NET assembly in a native terminal without debugging, with interactive stdin. Uses the saved profile and optional overrides. The terminal and its processes persist until explicitly closed or the workspace/IDE exits.

cwd.description: Workspace document reference; not a temporary input artifact.

operations.name: Debug Continue
operations.description: Continue the paused debuggee.

operations.name: Debug Pause
operations.description: Pause the running debuggee and asynchronously inspect its actual threads/stack.

operations.name: Debug Next
operations.description: Step over the current source statement in the selected thread.

operations.name: Debug Step In
operations.description: Step into a function through DAP.

operations.name: Debug Step Out
operations.description: Step out of the selected function through DAP.

operations.name: Debug Stop
operations.description: Stop the debug session. Terminates launched debuggees and their owned terminals; detaches from an explicitly attached process, leaving that existing process running.

operations.name: Debug Evaluate
operations.description: Evaluate an expression or debugger console command in the selected stopped frame. Expressions/console commands can have side effects in the target process.

operations.name: Debug Variables
operations.description: Read a bounded page of children from a live stopped-frame variable reference. References become stale on resume.

operations.name: Debug Frame
operations.description: Select a current stack frame and refresh its scopes, locals and watches.

operations.name: Debug Thread
operations.description: Select a current thread and inspect its stack.

operations.name: Debug Source
operations.description: Read an adapter-issued source reference while paused, including generated disassembly. This is a read-only view; it does not broaden editable workspace paths.

operations.name: Terminal Create
operations.description: Start a persistent interactive shell in this IDE workspace. Uses native ConPTY/PTY, not a one-shot command. Sessions survive the Core job and must be closed explicitly; closing the IDE/workspace terminates their processes.

cwd.description: Workspace document reference; not a temporary input artifact.

operations.name: Terminal List
operations.description: List this IDE instance’s persistent terminal sessions, including user-created sessions. Requires process access because terminal data can include output beyond project documents.

operations.name: Terminal Read
operations.description: Read a bounded terminal screen/scrollback range as plain Unicode lines. Coordinates are zero-based display cells, not LSP positions. Output belongs to the live terminal, not this job’s artifact workspace.

operations.name: Terminal Write
operations.description: Write raw UTF-8/control input to an existing interactive terminal. A carriage return submits a shell line. This can execute arbitrary commands with the IDE user’s permissions.

operations.name: Terminal Key
operations.description: Send an interactive terminal key. Modifier bits: Shift=1, Alt=2, Ctrl=4.

operations.name: Terminal Resize
operations.description: Resize a persistent PTY and its emulated screen.

operations.name: Terminal Clear
operations.description: Clear retained scrollback without restarting the shell or changing files.

operations.name: Terminal Close
operations.description: Terminate and remove one terminal and its process tree. Closing the panel only hides it; this operation ends the session.

operations.description: Read semantic color classifications from the shared language server and current live document. Requires the expected revision; rejects concurrent document changes. Positions/lengths use UTF-16; glyphStart/glyphEnd are Unicode-codepoint indexes. supported=false means lexical fallback. Data is bounded to 50,000 tokens or 4 MiB and reports truncation. C# requires prior language_configure; inspection never enables it.
